I think that his advice is not valuable to most of us. Someone in his position can afford to learn cell therapy, nuclear fusion and things like that just out of curiosity, most of us who are trying to make a living cannot. My advice to youngsters would be as follows:
1. Find an area where you have good talent. If it involves physical work, better, since it would be difficult for AI to replace you. 
2. Keep learning AI and it's use cases in free time. If time permits, do some passion project, AI related.
3. Learn about financial management as much as possible. Invest money really well. Try to be financially independent ASAP. 
4. If need comes, don't be scared to move to a completely new field and start from scratch. Example: You are a software engineer, who wants to move to carpentry and make a small business out of it in his/her native place.
I believe, if all the AI hype lives up to it, society will undergo abrupt changes. Stability will be very less, so it's better to embrace it. If you are from India, you can also prepare for government jobs if you are scared of uncertainty. Good luck!
